evidence: Measured in 1 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.14% of total volatiles (0.028mg per chew).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Caryophyllenyl alcohol is a botanical compound known as a terpene alcohol, sharing a close structural relationship with the spicy, woody molecule beta-caryophyllene. It contributes to the complex aromatic profiles of certain plant essential oils, where it is extracted through careful distillation. People most likely encounter it as a trace element in the scent of hemp and other aromatic herbs.
consumer_summary.found_in: It is notably found in the essential oils of hemp (Cannabis) and the herbaceous plant Sonchus asper, commonly known as spiny sowthistle.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to caryophyllenyl alcohol to understand how trace components in essential oils contribute to a plant's natural defenses. Early laboratory research (Oxford level 5, in vitro) is exploring its potential role as an antimicrobial agent, particularly when it is concentrated through specific distillation techniques. Scientists are interested in whether this molecule might offer new ways to inhibit bacterial growth.

structure_function.statement: Early work points toward caryophyllenyl alcohol supporting natural defenses against certain microbes.
structure_function.basis: This rests on a single laboratory study evaluating the antimicrobial activity of hemp essential oil fractions.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether caryophyllenyl alcohol can effectively inhibit the growth of bacteria like Staphylococcus aureus. If this bears out, it could eventually inspire new botanical preservatives or topical formulations.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: An animal model of topical bacterial infection comparing a caryophyllenyl alcohol ointment against a standard antibacterial and a placebo over 14 days, measuring bacterial load reduction and tissue healing.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far is early laboratory research (Oxford level 5); the molecule has not yet been evaluated in human or animal trials.
